question: Can a threshold chosen only from the prior-year calibration windows, with a rule fixed in advance, reach a better precision/recall trade than the existing window-recall 0.95 rule without exceeding the recall tolerance?
data_rule: Each rule sees only the calibration windows of the year before the evaluation year (the original annual_fold calibration role) and their labels. Earlier years were training data of the same models and are in-sample, so they are not used. Evaluation windows and labels are not read until thresholds for every rule are written to disk and hashed.

control.note: Existing rule; must reproduce the stored thresholds exactly.

selection: Window rules use helio24.calibration.recall_threshold on calibrated calibration probabilities. Run rules use the same grid and tie order: among distinct calibrated calibration probabilities with calibration positive-run recall at or above the target, take the fewest calibration false-alarm windows, then the larger threshold. A positive run is consecutive-hour positive-labelled windows of one HARP and is alarmed when any window is at or above the threshold.

arms.baseline_gate: Baseline calibration probabilities are recomputed by inference with the stored frozen models and must reproduce the stored baseline threshold under control_w95 in every year. If any year fails, baseline is excluded and reported as not evaluable, and chronological becomes primary. No retraining.
arms.tcn_arms: Calibrated seed-ensemble probabilities from the stored per-seed calibration scores and calibrators; control_w95 must reproduce stored thresholds.

acceptance.all_year_primary: per_year_primary holds in all six positive years for the same rule
acceptance.zero_positive_2018: Report thresholds, false-alarm windows and episodes only; recall-based conditions are not applicable.
acceptance.result_meaning: A pass justifies only a separate prospective protocol. It never changes alerts, thresholds or models.

inference: Paired full-HARP bootstrap (1000 draws, seed 24) of episode precision and FP-window differences versus control, conditional on the frozen selected thresholds. It does not include uncertainty from the threshold selection itself.
disclosure: Targets 0.93 and 0.90 and the run-level basis were chosen after seeing the threshold tradeoff results: fixed multipliers broke recall in 2016 and 2023, and an oracle threshold had headroom inside the recall tolerance. They were not tuned on any selection-rule result; none had been computed when this file was frozen.
scope: Adaptive development on already inspected years, not an independent test. Counts are overlapping forecast windows and groupings of them, not physical flares.
prohibitions: No evaluation labels or outcomes in any selection rule
No other targets, bases, multipliers, persistence or combined rules after seeing results
